Alloying of Mo and C in the matrix enhances solid solution strengthening. C atoms ﬁll interstitial sites of the matrix and induce interstitial strengthening. Mo has a larger atomic size than the other alloying elements and intensiﬁes lattice distortion by ﬁlling substitutional sites, leading to additional solid solution strengthening as well

Hard M6C particles in grain interiors impede the movement of dislocations, and therefore induce precipitation strengthening. M23C6 carbides are also known to induce bowing of dislocations and Orowan strengthening, as the carbides are incoherent with the FCC HEA matrix

The carbides located in grain boundaries act as obstacles for grain growth by the Zener pinning effect, keeping reﬁned grains. As a result, the grains are ﬁner with a few micrometer-scaled average grain sizes. The reﬁnement of the grains leads to further blocking of dislocation movement, resulting in grain boundary strengthening governed by Hall-Petch relationship
Microstructural characterization of the alloys after tensile deformation in Fig. 4 helps further understanding of the transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) behavior at cryogenic temperature.
This proves that deformation-induced phase transformation from FCC to BCC was activated mainly at 77 K by lower FCC stability at cryogenic temperature.
